newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to begin advanced jet trainer development.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to begin advanced jet trainer development.

text.p: The South Korean government has decided to begin full-scale development of the KTX-2 advanced jet-trainer/light-combat aircraft programme, the Ministry of National Defense said on Thursday.

A ministry statement said the development programme would begin in the second half of 1997 for scheduled completion in 2005. The aircraft would initially be delivered to the Korean Air Force in late 2005.
It said the decision was announced at a meeting of Prime Minister Koh Kun, related ministers and research heads.
The programme, which would also include participation by private companies, is expected to cost $2 billion.

The ministry also said the programme would involve 6,000 employees annually from 12 domestic firms including Samsung Aerospace Industries Co and Lockheed Martin Corp of the U.S in design and production.
